# Results — Study 421 (Williams Alligator) on real daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Bill Williams' Alligator
(three displaced SMMAs of the median price: Jaw 13/8, Teeth 8/5, Lips 5/3) turned into a
long/flat and long/short daily timing rule and raced — NET, excess-of-cash vs
excess-of-cash — against buy-and-hold and against the simplest trend benchmark, SMA(200).
Tested on SPY daily total-return closes from 1993-01-29 to 2026-06-23 (the last complete
trading day; today's partial bar dropped). One-way cost = 5 bps on NAV; short leg pays
50 bps/yr borrow; cash leg credited at 4%/yr flat (FRED unavailable). One documented
execution lag (signal at the close of t acts on the return t→t+1). As-of **2026-06-24**.*

## Data stamp

| Ticker | Window | n days | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|---|
| SPY | 1993-01-29 → 2026-06-23 | 8,406 | `6e7b9258f0b0` |

## The three-way race — buy-and-hold vs Alligator vs SMA(200) (long/flat, net @ 5 bps)

| Arm | CAGR | Sharpe | Vol | Max drawdown | HAC *t* (mean daily) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **Buy-and-hold** | **+10.78%** | +0.551 | 18.6% | **−55.19%** | +3.66 |
| **Alligator long/flat** | +6.46% | +0.593 | 10.6% | −20.37% | +3.79 |
| **SMA(200) benchmark** | +9.12% | **+0.726** | 12.0% | −21.91% | +4.50 |

- **Alligator vs buy-and-hold:** Sharpe-difference HAC *t* = **−1.71** — below the
  |*t*| ≥ 2 bar, and *negative*: the Alligator earns a **lower mean daily return** than
  buy-and-hold. Its slightly higher Sharpe (+0.593 vs +0.551) is pure volatility
  reduction (it sits in cash 41% of the time), not timing skill.
- **Alligator vs SMA(200):** Sharpe-difference HAC *t* = **−1.61** — the simpler one-line
  rule has the *higher* Sharpe (+0.726 vs +0.593) **and** the higher CAGR (+9.12% vs
  +6.46%). The three-displaced-line machinery is strictly dominated by a single moving
  average on this tape.
- **In-position fraction:** 59.1% of trading days long SPY; 40.9% in cash. **497** position
  changes over 33 years (~15/yr) — more turnover than the SMA(200) rule, for a worse result.

## Permutation placebo (long/flat)

A circular-block (21-day) shuffle keeps the Alligator's *exposure profile* but destroys its
*timing*, re-raced vs buy-and-hold 2,000 times:

| Observed Sharpe-diff vs B&H | Placebo mean | *p*-value |
|--:|--:|--:|
| +0.042 | ≈ +0.05 | **0.151** |

A trend-agnostic reshuffle of the same in/out pattern beats buy-and-hold by as much as the
real signal **15% of the time** — the signature of an exposure effect, not a timing edge.

## Long/short arm (net @ 5 bps, 50 bps/yr borrow)

| Arm | CAGR | Sharpe | Vol | Max drawdown | HAC *t* | diff-*t* vs B&H |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Alligator long/short | +2.69% | +0.156 | 17.0% | −37.48% | +1.05 | −1.85 |

Adding the short leg makes it *worse*: the bearish-fan shorts get whipsawed and pay borrow.
In-position 82.8% of days, 873 position changes.

## Cost sensitivity (Alligator long/flat)

| One-way cost | Sharpe | CAGR | Max drawdown |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 0 bps (gross) | +0.664 | +7.26% | −18.76% |
| 1 bps | +0.650 | +7.10% | −19.09% |
| 5 bps | +0.593 | +6.46% | −20.37% |
| 10 bps | +0.522 | +5.67% | −21.95% |
| 25 bps | +0.309 | +3.34% | −26.85% |

Even **gross** (0 bps) the Alligator's Sharpe (+0.664) is **below** the SMA(200) benchmark
(+0.726). There is no cost level at which the Alligator is the best choice.

## Synthetic positive control (long/short, planted multi-week trends)

A deterministic tape (seed 421, n=4,000) with *planted* symmetric directional runs. The
``edge`` knob scales the planted trend; ``edge = 0`` is an i.i.d. null.

| Tape | BH Sharpe | Alligator Sharpe | Alligator HAC *t* | diff-*t* vs BH |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| Null (edge = 0) | +0.179 | +0.357 | +1.44 | +0.42 |
| Trend (edge = 1.5) | −0.130 | +1.999 | +6.97 | +4.75 |

The engine is **faithful**: it raises no false alarm on the i.i.d. null (diff-*t* = +0.42)
and clearly detects a planted trend (diff-*t* = +4.75, HAC *t* = +6.97). The real-tape null
is therefore a genuine "no harvestable trend in SPY", not a broken detector. *(This is a
machinery proof only — it never backs the real-tape Signal stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — WEAK.** The Alligator's edge over buy-and-hold does not clear the inference
  bar (Sharpe-difference HAC *t* = −1.71, and negative on the mean return; permutation
  *p* = 0.151). Its only robust effect is vol/drawdown reduction — a generic de-risking
  outcome shared by every slow trend filter. Long/short is weaker still (*t* = +1.05).
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** Net of costs the Alligator earns *less* than buy-and-hold
  (+6.46% vs +10.78% CAGR) and is strictly dominated by a one-line SMA(200) on every axis
  (Sharpe-difference *t* = −1.61 against the simpler rule). Three displaced averages buy
  nothing a single average doesn't do better and cheaper.
- **Does the waking alligator catch trends? — NOT SUPPORTED.** It catches *crashes* (by
  being out of the market on sustained downtrends), not *trends* (by being in at the right
  time). The placebo and the faithful synthetic control together show the effect is reduced
  exposure, not the "wake and eat" timing the folklore promises.
